skill.summary: Inspect, automate, and debug local web applications with Playwright.
skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: The helper executes caller-provided server strings through a shell and runs an unrestricted follow-up command. Most SKILL.md backtick alerts are Markdown false positives, but the instructions discourage source inspection before executing the helper.

remediation.issue: The server helper passes caller-provided strings to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Accept argument arrays, use shell=False, and reject shell operators unless the user explicitly approves them.

remediation.issue: The helper executes an unrestricted trailing command.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation and display the exact executable and arguments before running the command.

remediation.issue: The documentation tells agents to execute the helper before reading its source.
remediation.suggestion: Remove anti-inspection language and encourage users to review community scripts before execution.

remediation.issue: Screenshots use predictable shared temporary file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Create private temporary files with unique names and restrictive permissions, then remove them after use.

remediation.issue: Captured browser console data is written to a fixed output file.
remediation.suggestion: Warn that console messages may contain secrets, redact sensitive values, and avoid overwriting existing artifacts.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Applications with Playwright
content.value_statement: Local web interfaces can fail in ways that static code review misses. This skill guides Playwright inspection, interaction, screenshots, and console capture.
actual_capabilities: Launches headless Chromium through synchronous Python Playwright scripts.
Waits for dynamic pages to finish network activity before inspection.
Discovers visible buttons, links, and form controls from the rendered page.
Captures full-page screenshots and browser console messages.
Starts one or more local development servers and stops them after testing.
Automates local static HTML files through file URLs.
limitations: The examples require Python, Playwright, and an installed Chromium browser.
The bundled helper executes local commands and requires careful review before use.
Example URLs, selectors, file paths, and form values require project-specific changes.
The skill provides examples, not a complete assertion framework or test suite.

use_cases.title: Verify a Frontend Change
use_cases.description: Open a local application, exercise the changed workflow, and capture visible results for review.

use_cases.title: Investigate a UI Failure
use_cases.description: Inspect rendered elements, browser console messages, and screenshots to identify a failing interaction.

use_cases.title: Review a Local Prototype
use_cases.description: Run a repeatable browser walkthrough and document the behavior of a static or dynamic prototype.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [local URL] in headless Chromium. Wait for network activity to settle, then list visible buttons, links, and form controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner inspection of a running local application

prompt_templates.title: Test a User Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test [workflow] at [local URL]. Perform each step, report failures, and capture a screenshot after the final action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Functional verification of one user journey

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Browser Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce [issue] at [local URL]. Capture browser console messages, note failed interactions, and summarize likely causes with supporting observations.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Servers and Regression Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the bundled helper first. With approval, start [server commands], test [workflows], collect screenshots and console evidence, then verify server cleanup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced testing across multiple local services

output_examples.input: Inspect the local dashboard and report available interactions.
output: The dashboard loaded after network activity settled.
Visible controls included Add project, Search, Settings, and Sign out.
Two links lacked descriptive text and need accessibility review.

output_examples.input: Test the local sign-in flow and capture browser errors.
output: The sign-in form accepted the supplied test account.
Submission remained on the sign-in page instead of opening the dashboard.
The browser console reported one failed authentication request.
A screenshot was captured after the failed submission.

output_examples.input: Verify a static contact form from a local HTML file.
output: The page opened from the local file.
Name and email fields accepted the test values.
The submit action completed without a visible confirmation message.

best_practices: Review every community script and the exact command arguments before execution.
Use stable role, label, or identifier selectors and wait for meaningful page states.
Use test accounts and redact secrets from screenshots and console logs.
anti_patterns: Do not run unreviewed server strings through a shell.
Do not rely only on fixed delays when a page offers observable readiness signals.
Do not store sensitive screenshots or console logs in predictable shared paths.

faq.question: What does this skill test?
faq.answer: It supports browser interaction, rendered element inspection, screenshots, and console capture for local web applications.

faq.question: Does it start local development servers?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled helper can start multiple servers, wait for their ports, run a command, and stop the servers.

faq.question: Which browser automation library does it use?
faq.answer: The examples use the synchronous Python API for Playwright with headless Chromium.

faq.question: Can it test static HTML files?
faq.answer: Yes. An example opens a local HTML file through a file URL and performs browser interactions.

faq.question: Does it create a complete automated test suite?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that require project-specific selectors, assertions, paths, and test data.

faq.question: What should I review before running it?
faq.answer: Inspect the helper source, server commands, target URLs, output paths, test credentials, and data that screenshots or logs may capture.
